newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan says not reviewing investment due to EMU.
newsitem.headline: Nissan says not reviewing investment due to EMU.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday that it was not reviewing its global investment strategy, including the status of its base in Britain, over the issue of European economic and monetary union.
A company spokeswoman told Reuters that Nissan has no intention now to change Britain's status as an important base for Nissan to supply cars to the rest of Europe and elsewhere.

"Britain is an important car supply base on the global level. So we have absolutely no intention now to change that status," she said in a telephone interview. "We are not reviewing our investment strategy now as a result of the Euro (single European currency) issue."

She added that the company has a production capacity of 300,000 units annually in Britain and the cars produced there are sold not only to the British market but also in continental Europe as well as other areas such as Japan and Africa.
She also said the company would continue to attach importance to its factories in Britain.

Asked whether Nissan will review its investment strategy in the Britain if London stayed out of European monetary union, the spokeswoman declined comment, adding that it was hard to know what kind of conclusion will be made in Europe.
"Even if we were to consider building factories in other areas, we want to take advantage of the active investment we made in offshore production bases in the past," she said.
"We will continue to attach importance to our factories in Britain," she said.
Nissan, Japan's second biggest carmaker, announced earlier this month that it would invest a further 215 million sterling to build a third new car model at its plant in Sunderland, northeast England.
Nissan said the addition to its production line at Nissan Motor Mfg (UK) Ltd (NMUK) would create 800 direct new jobs by the year 2000. In Europe, Nissan has production units in Britain and Spain.
